# Cppcheck

Cppcheck is a static analysis tool for C and C++ code.

## About

Cppcheck is an analysis tool for C/C++ code. It provides unique code analysis to detect bugs and focuses on detecting undefined behaviour and dangerous coding constructs. The goal is to detect only real errors in the code, and generate as few false positives (wrongly reported warnings) as possible.

Despite the name, Cppcheck is designed for both C and C++.

## What Cppcheck Can Detect

The kinds of bugs that can be found with Cppcheck include:

- Undefined behavior
- Using dangerous code patterns
- Coding style issues

## Limitations

Static analysis tools like Cppcheck do not have human knowledge about what your program is intended to do. If the output from your program is valid but unexpected, this will typically not be detected. Static analysis should be used as a complement to other quality assurance methods including careful design, testing, dynamic analysis, and fuzzing.

## Usage

### GUI

The tool provides a graphical user interface for interactive analysis. You can create project files and configure various analysis options.

The GUI can import:
- Visual Studio solution / project
- Compile database (generated from CMake/qbs/etc)
- Borland C++ Builder 6

### Command Line

#### Basic Usage

To check a single file:
```
cppcheck file.c
```

#### Checking All Files in a Directory

To recursively check all source files in a directory:
```
cppcheck path
```

#### Example

Given this simple code in `file1.c`:
```c
int main()
{
    char a[10];
    a[10] = 0;
    return 0;
}
```

Running `cppcheck file1.c` will output:
```
Checking file1.c...
[file1.c:4]: (error) Array 'a[10]' index 10 out of bounds
```

## Manual

A complete manual is available online at: https://cppcheck.sourceforge.io/manual.pdf

## Webpage

https://cppcheck.sourceforge.io/

## License

Cppcheck is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

# Introduction

Cppcheck is an analysis tool for C/C++ code. It provides unique code analysis to detect bugs and focuses on detecting undefined behaviour and dangerous coding constructs. The goal is to detect only real errors in the code, and generate as few false positives (wrongly reported warnings) as possible. Cppcheck is designed to analyze your C/C++ code even if it has non-standard syntax, as is common in for example embedded projects.

Supported code and platforms:

- Cppcheck checks non-standard code that contains various compiler extensions, inline assembly code, etc.
- Cppcheck is cross platform and is used in various posix/windows/etc environments.

The checks in Cppcheck are not perfect. There are bugs that should be found, that Cppcheck fails to detect.

## About static analysis

The kinds of bugs that you can find with static analysis are:

- Undefined behavior
- Using dangerous code patterns
- Coding style

There are many bugs that you can not find with static analysis. Static analysis tools do not have human knowledge about what your program is intended to do. If the output from your program is valid but unexpected then in most cases this is not detected by static analysis tools. For instance, if your small program writes "Helo" on the screen instead of "Hello" it is unlikely that any tool will complain about that.

Static analysis should be used as a complement in your quality assurance. It does not replace any of:

- Careful design
- Testing
- Dynamic analysis
- Fuzzing

# Getting started

## GUI

It is not required but creating a new project file is a good first step. There are a few options you can tweak to get good results.

In the project settings dialog, the first option you see is "Import project". It is recommended that you use this feature if you can. Cppcheck can import:

- Visual studio solution / project
- Compile database, which can be generated from CMake/qbs/etc build files
- Borland C++ Builder 6

When you have filled out the project settings and clicked on OK, the Cppcheck analysis will start.

## Command line

### First test

Here is some simple code:

    int main()
    {
        char a[10];
        a[10] = 0;
        return 0;
    }

If you save that into file1.c and execute:

    cppcheck file1.c

The output from Cppcheck will then be:

    Checking file1.c...
    [file1.c:4]: (error) Array 'a[10]' index 10 out of bounds

### Checking all files in a folder

Normally a program has many source files. Cppcheck can check all source files in a directory:

    cppcheck path

If "path" is a folder, then Cppcheck will recursively check all source files in this folder:

    Checking path/file1.cpp...
    1/2 files checked 50% done
    Checking path/file2.cpp...
    2/2 files checked 100% done

# Command line options

For a complete list of command line options, run:

    cppcheck --help

## Basic Options

- `--enable=<id>` - Enable additional checks
- `--error-exitcode=<n>` - Exit code if errors are found
- `--inline-suppr` - Enable inline suppressions
- `--quiet` - Only print error messages
- `--verbose` - More detailed output
- `-j <jobs>` - Number of threads to use

## Output Options

- `--xml` - Write results in XML format
- `--template=<format>` - Format the output using a template

# More Information

For complete documentation, visit: https://cppcheck.sourceforge.io/

run(["-i","*.c","."])
run(["--file-filter=*.c","."])

import subprocess,os,tempfile
def run(sup_content,args_extra=[]):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir="/tmp")
    open(os.path.join(d,"t.c"),"w").write("int main(){char a[10]; a[10]=0;}")
    open(os.path.join(d,"sup.txt"),"w").write(sup_content)
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--suppressions-list=sup.txt"]+args_extra+["t.c"],cwd=d,capture_output=True,text=True)
    print(repr(sup_content),r.returncode,repr(r.stdout),repr(r.stderr))
run("arrayIndexOutOfBounds\n")
run("# comment\narrayIndexOutOfBounds // trailing\n")
run("// comment\narrayIndexOutOfBounds\n")
run(" arrayIndexOutOfBounds \n")
run("\n\narrayIndexOutOfBounds:t.c:1\n")
run(":t.c\n")
run("invalid suppression line with spaces\n")
# xml suppressions variants
import subprocess
def runxml(content):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir="/tmp")
    open(os.path.join(d,"t.c"),"w").write("int main(){char a[10]; a[10]=0;}")
    open(os.path.join(d,"sup.xml"),"w").write(content)
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","--suppress-xml=sup.xml","t.c"],cwd=d,capture_output=True,text=True)

runxml('not xml')
runxml('<suppressions><suppress><id></id></suppress></suppressions>')
runxml('<suppressions></suppressions>')

    def pass_unused_vars(self):
        if not self.settings.is_enabled('style'):
            return
        toks=self.tu.tokens
        # Build use info per var from ctx.token_var and assignment events and read_events. Read_events from env walk only covers executes branches etc but token_var gives lexical all.
        # Classify occurrences lexically
        # Map assignment events from exec by var id (+ elem display for elements)
        # Determine for each local var:
        for var in self.ctx.locals:
            if var.is_param: continue
            if not var.name: continue
            occ=[idx for idx,v in self.ctx.token_var.items() if v is var]
            # Declaration names aren't in token_var
            # Classify occ: is there any read/value use? We can look at read_events scalar/array_base/address/member kinds.
            reads=[e for e in self.read_events if e['var'] is var]
            assign_events=[e for e in self.assignment_events if e.get('var') is var and e.get('kind') in ('var','incdec')]
            elem_events=[e for e in self.assignment_events if e.get('var') is var and e.get('kind')=='elem']
            # Used for unusedVariable: any occurrence (including writes to elements / taking address / assignments?) For int x; (no occ/read/assign) unused.
            has_occurrence=len(occ)>0 or len(elem_events)>0
            # Address taken counts as use (read event kind address)
            if not has_occurrence and not assign_events:
                # But if var has an initializer, assign_events includes it, then it's unread not unused.
                tok=var.name_tok
                self.add_error(Error('unusedVariable','style',f"Unused variable: {var.name}",[Loc(tok.file,tok.line,tok.col,'')],symbol=var.name),require=['style'])
                continue
            # unassigned: used (has read occurrence of scalar kind) and no plain assignment/initialization to it. Initializer counts as assign_events is_decl_init with op at name for direct init etc; var.init_range presence also counts.
            has_assign=len(assign_events)>0 or var.init_range is not None
            # ++/-- events are assignments for unread but not counted as value assignment for unassigned. Exclude incdec from has_assign.
            has_value_assign=any(e.get('kind')=='var' for e in assign_events) or var.init_range is not None
            scalar_reads=[e for e in reads if e['kind'] in ('scalar','member')]
            if scalar_reads and not has_value_assign and not var.is_array:
                tok=var.name_tok
                self.add_error(Error('unassignedVariable','style',f"Variable '{var.name}' is not assigned a value.",[Loc(tok.file,tok.line,tok.col,'')],symbol=var.name),require=['style'])
            # unread + redundant for simple vars: chronological events interleaved with reads by token index.
            # Build timeline of assign/read events for this var sorted by token position. Reads from token_var classified lexically may be more reliable than read_events (env walk may have branches). Use lex classification below for timeline.
            timeline=self._var_timeline(var)
            # redundantAssignment: pairs consecutive assignments with no reads between, first is not decl init, values differ (known_after if available/rhs text diff)
            # unread: assignment whose value never read before next assignment or end, except if that next assignment triggered redundantAssignment for it (then skip unread for earlier assignment)
            redundant_earlier=set()

                            prim=Loc(op_tok.file,op_tok.line,op_tok.col,f"{var.name} is overwritten")
                            locs=[Loc(prev_tok.file,prev_tok.line,prev_tok.col,f"{var.name} is assigned"), prim]
                            self.add_error(Error('redundantAssignment','style',f"Variable '{var.name}' is reassigned a value before the old one has been used.",locs,symbol=var.name),require=['style'])
                            redundant_earlier.add(id(ev))
            for ev in timeline:

    print(f"\n{passed} passed, {failed} failed"); print(fails)

        ["--template={file}:{line} {message}","--template-location={file}:{line}:{column}: note: {info}\\n{code}"],
        ["--report-type=misra-c-2012"],["--report-type=misra-cpp-2023"],["--report-type=cert-c-2016"],["--report-type=cert-cpp-2016"],["--report-type=autosar"],
        ["--report-type=misra-c-2012","--xml"],["--report-type=cert-c-2016","--xml"],
        ["--inconclusive","--enable=all"],["--check-level=reduced"],["--check-level=exhaustive"],
        ["--std=c89"],["--std=c++03"],["--platform=win32A"],["--platform=unix32"],["--platform=unspecified"],
    ]:
        case(f"{name} {args}",{fn:code},args+[fn])
# inconclusive specific patterns
inconc=[
 ("arraycond","void f(int i){int a[10]; if(i<20) a[i]=0;}"),
 ("nullpossible","void f(int *p){if(p) *p=1; else *p=2;}"),
 ("uninitbranch","int f(int c){int x; if(c) x=1; return x;}"),
 ("ptroob","void f(int *p){p[10]=0;}"),
 ("buffercopy","void f(char *d, char *s){strcpy(d,s);}"),
 ("arraythen","void f(int *a,int i){a[i]=0; if(i<10) return;}"),
 ("suspicioussemi","void f(int x){if(x); return;}"),
 ("dupbranch","int f(int x){if(x) return 1; else return 1;}"),
 ("constcond","int f(int x){if(x<5 && x>10) return 1; return 0;}"),
]
for n,c in inconc:
    for a in [[],["--inconclusive"],["--enable=all"],["--enable=all","--inconclusive"]]:
        case(f"inc {n} {a}",{"test.c":c},a+["test.c"])
def run(cmd,files,args):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(dir='/tmp')
    for n,cn in files.items():
        p=os.path.join(d,n); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True); open(p,'w').write(cn)
    try:
        r=subprocess.run(cmd+args,cwd=d,capture_output=True,text=True,timeout=10,env={**os.environ,'CPPCHECK_IMPL_DEBUG':'1'}); return r.returncode,r.stdout,r.stderr
    except Exception as e: return -999,'',str(e)
    finally: shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True)
def main():
    filt=sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else ''; p=f=0; fails=[]
    for name,files,args in cases:
        if filt and filt not in name: continue
        ref=run([REF],files,args); mine=run(MINE,files,args)
        if ref==mine: p+=1
        else:
            f+=1; fails.append(name); print(f"\n=== {name}")
            if ref[1]!=mine[1]: print('OUT\n'+''.join(difflib.unified_diff(ref[1].splitlines(True),mine[1].splitlines(True))))
            if ref[2]!=mine[2]: print('ERR\n'+''.join(difflib.unified_diff(ref[2].splitlines(True),mine[2].splitlines(True))))
            if ref[0]!=mine[0]: print('exit',ref[0],mine[0])
    print(f"\n{p} passed {f} failed"); print(fails[:100])
if __name__=='__main__': main()
